text: I want to make every other row in the assets grid light green.

Use a CSS zebra-striping rule on the Assets table body.

1) Add a class to the table in `Views/Assets/Index.cshtml`:


```razor
<table class="table assets-grid">
```


2) Add this to `wwwroot/css/site.css`:


```css
.assets-grid tbody tr:nth-child(even) {
  background-color: #e8f5e9; /* light green */
}
```


That will make every other data row light green (header row is unaffected).

text: what happens to the database record when I delete the record

In your current code, deleting an asset is a **hard delete**.

From `AssetsController.DeleteConfirmed`:
- It finds the row by `AssetId`
- Calls `_context.Assets.Remove(asset)`
- Calls `SaveChangesAsync()`

So the record is physically removed from the `Assets` table (not marked inactive, not soft-deleted).

Also:
- If the asset is not found, nothing is deleted.
- There is no custom archive/audit logic in this action.
- Based on your EF model, `Asset` references lookup tables (`AssetType`, `User`, etc.), but no dependent child entities are configured under `Asset`, so deleting an asset should just remove that one row.
